LESSON: WRITING 5.4.1 • HANDWRITING/ BRAILLE WRITING •

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade one
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 5
Topic 5.4: Writing 5.4.1 • Handwriting/ Braille writing •
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 5.4.1 • Handwriting/ Braille writing •, part of Strand 5 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade one ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: How can we tell letters are correctly written?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 5.4.1 • Handwriting/ Braille writing • together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Learning to learn- The learner’s ability to build relationships is promoted as they play language games with peers involving the shaping or marking of

letters.

Values:
Unity is enhanced as the learner collaborates with others during language game activities.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills (self -esteem): Learner acquires high level of self-esteem as they write legibly for effective communication.

Links to other Learning Areas:
The learner applies the writing legibly and neatly or make dots in all learning areas.

52

Suggested learning resources

• Braille letter cards,

• Slate and stylus,

• Audio, video clip,

• Textbooks in braille and in appropriate font and colour contrast.
